name: Repository SSH Setup + Usage Completer
sprintRole: Complete and verify repository SSH transport/authentication, then teach the operator the exact ongoing Git usage for the verified repository
useWhen: An existing or newly resolved Git repository needs SSH transport configured, repaired, converted from HTTPS, or proven for fetch/pull/push, and the operator also needs to know how to use the completed setup afterward.
inspectFirst: Actual OS/shell/runtime, verified repository root and remotes, Git host/provider, current branch/HEAD/status, SSH tool and key inventory, agent state, existing SSH config/known_hosts, provider authentication/key registration, access intent, repository permissions, network/policy state, and current task.
expectedOutput: A completed or precisely blocked SSH setup with preserved keys/config/remotes, verified provider registration and host trust, fail-fast repository read proof, safe write dry-run when read-write access requires it, exact remote/key evidence without secret exposure, and a tailored HOW TO USE THIS SSH SETUP guide.
nextStep: Use the now-verified SSH repository path for the requested Git/repository task; when a genuine user-only provider/passphrase/browser gate remains, perform that one exact action and resume at the first unproven SSH layer rather than restarting setup.
proofGate: Repository identity and shell are grounded; private key/passphrase contents never leave the local credential boundary; existing keys/config/remotes are preserved unless specifically owned; all applicable SSH layers are completed; git ls-remote succeeds noninteractively; read-write intent receives safe write-authorization proof when practical or an explicit ceiling; and the final response explains exact ongoing clone/fetch/pull/push/test usage.
copyContent:
COMPLETE THIS REPOSITORY'S SSH SETUP AND PROVE IT WORKS. THEN EXPLAIN EXACTLY HOW TO USE THE VERIFIED SSH SETUP. DO NOT STOP AT INSTRUCTIONS WHEN THE CURRENT ENVIRONMENT CAN PERFORM THE SETUP.

Repository: xyz_repo_url_owner_name_or_current_repo
Access intent: xyz_read_write_read_only_or_infer_from_task
Provider/account: xyz_provider_account_or_infer
Preferred existing key: xyz_key_path_or_auto_reuse_safe_existing

MISSION
Leave the requested Git repository using a verified SSH transport path for the access actually required. Preserve existing keys, SSH config, remotes, and unrelated work. Complete every agent-capable step now. After proof, give a short shell-correct HOW TO USE THIS SSH SETUP guide for clone/fetch/pull/push and key handling.

SUCCESS
Do not claim COMPLETE until every applicable layer is proven: exact repo/root and host; SSH tooling; suitable key pair; provider registration/authorization; host trust; correct SSH remote; bounded noninteractive repository read; safe write-authorization proof when push access is required; and the post-setup usage guide. Key generation, key upload, ssh -T, a remote URL change, or one successful fetch alone is not enough when a stronger applicable gate remains.

1. GROUND REPOSITORY + SHELL
- Detect OS, actual shell/runtime, current directory, Git/SSH availability, repository identity, and requested access.
- Git Bash/MSYS2 on Windows is not Linux. Never mix PowerShell cmdlets into Bash or POSIX syntax into PowerShell.
- For an existing checkout prove the root, then inspect git status --short --branch, current branch/HEAD, and git remote -v.
- Detect GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, enterprise Git, or another SSH-capable Git provider from evidence; do not assume GitHub.
- Preserve every unrelated remote.

2. REUSE OR CREATE KEY MATERIAL SAFELY
- Inspect the SSH directory, loaded identities, agent state, and relevant ~/.ssh/config before changing anything.
- Prefer a healthy suitable existing key over creating duplicate identities.
- PUBLIC KEY (.pub) may be registered with the provider. PRIVATE KEY must never be printed, pasted into chat, committed, uploaded, or exposed in logs.
- Never ask the operator to send a private key or passphrase in chat.
- Never overwrite an existing key file. If a new key is required, generate a provider-supported Ed25519 key at a non-colliding path; keep passphrase entry local. Do not silently create a passphrase-less key merely to avoid interaction.
- Do not delete old keys merely because a new one works.
- Load the selected identity into the platform SSH agent when required and state whether loading persists across terminal/reboot.
- Preserve existing SSH config. Add or change a Host stanza only when evidence requires it. Do not make a global Git/SSH-policy change when a per-repository remote or Host entry is sufficient.

3. REGISTER ONLY THE PUBLIC KEY
- Prefer an already authenticated provider CLI/API when it can register the public key without exposing credentials.
- For GitHub an authenticated gh session may register the public key; never print tokens or use --show-token.
- For GitLab, Bitbucket, enterprise Git, or another provider, use the supported account/repository key mechanism and verify whether that key type is read-only or write-capable.
- Never broaden permissions beyond the requested access intent.
- If browser/OAuth/passphrase/account consent is genuinely human-only, finish every safe local step first, then give ONE exact BLOCKED_USER_ONLY action involving only the public-key path or local unlock. Resume at the first unproven layer afterward.

4. VERIFY HOST TRUST
- Do not blindly answer yes to an unknown-host authenticity prompt.
- For a new host, compare its fingerprint with authoritative provider evidence before storing trust.
- Treat a changed-host-key warning as BLOCKED_HOST_TRUST until reconciled; never delete known_hosts entries merely to silence it.

5. CONFIGURE THIS REPOSITORY'S SSH REMOTE
- Derive the canonical SSH URL from verified provider/repository identity. Examples include git@github.com:OWNER/REPO.git, git@gitlab.com:OWNER/REPO.git, and git@bitbucket.org:WORKSPACE/REPO.git; use the provider's verified form.
- Preserve an already-correct SSH origin.
- If origin is HTTPS and SSH is the mission, change only origin with git remote set-url origin <verified-ssh-url> after key/provider readiness. Preserve unrelated remotes and intentional separate push URLs.
- Re-read git remote get-url origin and git remote -v and prove they identify the requested repository.

6. PROVE THE TRANSPORT FAIL-FAST
Use a bounded noninteractive repository read so bad SSH fails instead of looping password prompts.
- POSIX/Git Bash: GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=8' git ls-remote --heads origin
- PowerShell: set process-scoped GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and GIT_SSH_COMMAND=ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=8, run git ls-remote --heads origin, then restore only variables this prompt set.
Interpret failures by layer: publickey/password fallback = identity/registration; repository not found/access denied after SSH identity = repository permission/path; timeout/DNS/refused = BLOCKED_NETWORK_POLICY; host-key mismatch = BLOCKED_HOST_TRUST; malformed remote = URL/identity. Repair the identified layer before retrying.
ssh -T may assist diagnosis, but a provider may authenticate while returning a nonzero shell status. Prefer the repository git ls-remote result as the access proof.

7. PROVE WRITE AUTHORIZATION WHEN REQUIRED
- Read-only intent can close on the bounded read proof plus verified remote/key state.
- For read-write intent, confirm a normal branch and intended target without changing remote state.
- When safe run a non-mutating proof shaped as git push --dry-run origin HEAD:<verified-branch>. Do not create a remote branch, tag, commit, or force update merely to test credentials.
- If branch protection, detached HEAD, policy, or target state prevents safe dry-run proof, state that exact proof ceiling. Distinguish authentication from authorization to push to a particular branch.

8. PRECISE BLOCKERS
Use only the state supported by evidence: BLOCKED_USER_ONLY, BLOCKED_AUTHENTICATION, BLOCKED_PERMISSION, BLOCKED_NETWORK_POLICY, or BLOCKED_HOST_TRUST. Advance every other safe layer before stopping and give one exact continuation action.

9. HOW TO USE THIS SSH SETUP
After success emit this exact section heading: HOW TO USE THIS SSH SETUP. Tailor every command to values just proved. Explain that normal Git commands now use SSH automatically through the repository remote. Include the actual verified origin plus git remote get-url origin; git fetch origin; the repository-appropriate pull/update command; git push or git push -u origin <verified-branch> only when correct; future clone command git clone <verified-ssh-url>; the exact bounded git ls-remote test; public/private key paths without private contents; share/register the public key only and never share the private key or passphrase; any post-login agent-load action; and provider/branch-policy limitations separately from SSH failures.

FINAL REPORT
Report repository/root, OS/shell, provider/account when safely observable, access intent, key decision REUSED or GENERATED, public/private key paths without contents, provider registration, host trust, old/final remote, bounded read proof, write dry-run when applicable, COMPLETE or exact BLOCKED_* state, proof ceiling, HOW TO USE THIS SSH SETUP, and the first exact next action for the user's repository task.
